name: list_scheduled_task_projects
description: List projects that can be selected for iyw-claw scheduled tasks. Returns safe project ids and names without local paths. This is a read-only operation.

name: list_scheduled_tasks
description: Query iyw-claw scheduled tasks globally. Omit filters to list every active task across all projects; pass task_id for one task. This is a read-only operation.

project.description: Optional project absolute path or unique project name.

project_id.description: Optional project id from list_scheduled_task_projects. Do not combine with project.

name: create_scheduled_task
description: Create a global iyw-claw scheduled task. Omit project and project_id to use a dedicated persistent folder, or select a regular project. The current Agent is used by default. This operation executes immediately without a confirmation prompt.

project.description: Optional project absolute path or unique project name. Omit for a dedicated folder.

project_id.description: Optional project id from list_scheduled_task_projects. Do not combine with project.

prompt.description: Prompt executed on every scheduled run.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week.

timezone.description: IANA timezone, for example Asia/Shanghai. Defaults to UTC.

agent_type.description: Executor Agent. Defaults to the current Agent.

name: update_scheduled_task
description: Patch an existing iyw-claw scheduled task. Unspecified fields are preserved. This operation executes immediately without a confirmation prompt.

project.description: Project absolute path or unique project name.

project_id.description: Project id from list_scheduled_task_projects. Do not combine with project.

name: delete_scheduled_task
description: Delete an iyw-claw scheduled task by id. The task is disabled and soft-deleted while run history is retained. This operation executes immediately without a confirmation prompt.

name: browser_list_tabs
description: List every tab in iyw-claw's managed browser. All managed tabs are available to every Agent session. Read activeTabId for the current/default tab and tabs[].browserTabId for exact tab selection. Pass a browserTabId as tab_id to the other browser tools.

name: browser_open
description: Open an HTTP/HTTPS URL in iyw-claw's managed browser. By default this navigates activeTabId and does not add a tab. Pass tabs[].browserTabId as tab_id to navigate an exact tab. Set new_tab to true only when the user explicitly asks for another tab. If no tabs exist, the default call starts the browser and creates the first tab. All tabs use the same persistent profile and sign-in state, and the user can see and take over them.

new_tab.description: Create another tab instead of navigating the active tab. Do not combine with tab_id.

name: browser_snapshot
description: Read a fresh accessibility snapshot for one managed browser tab. The snapshot contains stable @eN references for browser_click and browser_fill; take another snapshot after navigation or material page changes.

name: browser_click
description: Click an element in a managed browser tab using an @eN reference from the latest browser_snapshot or a CSS selector. Human input preempts this operation.

name: browser_fill
description: Clear and fill an input in a managed browser tab using an @eN reference from the latest snapshot or a CSS selector. Never enter secrets unless the user explicitly supplied them for this task. Human input preempts this operation.

name: browser_press
description: Press a keyboard key or chord in a managed browser tab, for example Enter, Tab, Escape, or Control+a. Human input preempts this operation.

name: browser_scroll
description: Scroll a managed browser tab in one direction. Human input preempts this operation.

name: browser_wait
description: Wait for a selector to appear in a managed browser tab, or wait for a bounded number of milliseconds. Prefer a selector for deterministic page readiness.

name: browser_screenshot
description: Capture a screenshot of a managed browser tab into iyw-claw's managed browser screenshot directory. Returns the generated local path; use analyze_image when visual inspection is needed.

annotate.description: Overlay labels that correspond to snapshot references.

name: browser_close_tab
description: Close one managed browser tab. This closes the same visible tab for the user and every Agent session, so use it only when the tab is no longer needed.

name: present_task_files
description: Call this after creating task deliverables and before the final response. Register every produced file, directory, or HTTP/HTTPS URL so iyw-claw can show and preview it in the workspace Artifacts panel. Accepts working-directory-relative paths, absolute paths, and web URLs.

files.description: Files, directories, or HTTP/HTTPS URLs produced by this task. Relative paths resolve from the current working directory; absolute paths and web URLs are accepted.

name: delegate_to_agent
description: Hand off a self-contained sub-task to a separate local AI agent that runs in its own session. ASYNCHRONOUS: returns a task_id right away and the sub-agent keeps working in the background — this call never blocks. So you can fan out several delegations at once and keep working, then collect the results with get_delegation_status by passing the task_ids array (one id to poll a single task, or many at once to poll the whole fan-out in one call) — or stop one early with cancel_delegation(task_id). The sub-agent CANNOT see this conversation, your open files, or earlier turns — it starts cold, so `task` must carry everything it needs. Best for independent, parallelizable work you can describe up front; not for steps that need your ongoing back-and-forth.

agent_type.description: Which local agent runs the sub-task. Pick the one best suited to the work.

task.description: The complete, self-contained prompt for the sub-agent. It has no access to this conversation or your context, so spell out everything: the goal, the relevant background and absolute file paths, any constraints, and exactly what to return.

working_dir.description: Absolute path the sub-agent runs in. Defaults to this session's working directory.

name: get_delegation_status
description: Collect delegated task results — or check on them — by the task_ids from delegate_to_agent. Pass a single id in the array to poll one task, or many at once to poll a whole fan-out in a single call. The response is ALWAYS a JSON object {"tasks":[...]} with one entry per id, in the order you asked — one entry for a single id, several for a fan-out; every entry carries that task's task_id and status, so you can always tell which task it is and where it stands. The wait_ms argument picks the mode: omit it for a non-blocking snapshot (poll), or pass wait_ms to wait — wait_ms>0 blocks up to that many ms (capped at 60000; re-call to keep waiting), wait_ms=0 blocks with no timeout for as long as the sub-agent runs. When polling several, the wait returns as soon as ANY requested task reaches a terminal state, so re-call to keep collecting the rest. When you just need the results, prefer blocking over repeated polling. Each task reports its current state — running, or a terminal completed / failed / canceled (or unknown if the id isn't recognized); a finished task includes its full result text. While tasks are still running and you are simply waiting, do NOT emit any user-facing message between calls — just call again silently. Skip status narration like "still running", "not returned yet", or "continuing to wait"; it fragments the conversation. Speak to the user only when there is a terminal result to report or something genuinely needs their input.

task_ids.description: One or more task_ids returned by delegate_to_agent — pass a single id to poll one task, or several to poll them together in one call. The response is always a JSON object {"tasks":[...]} with one entry per id (in this order) — one entry for a single id — and each entry carries that task's task_id and status. With wait_ms set, the call returns as soon as ANY of these tasks reaches a terminal state.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait. Omit for an immediate snapshot (poll). A positive value blocks up to that many milliseconds (capped at 60000). 0 means no timeout — block until a task reaches a terminal state, however long it takes. When several ids are given, the wait resolves as soon as ANY requested task becomes terminal.

name: cancel_delegation
description: Stop a running delegated task by its task_id and tear down its sub-agent — use this only when you no longer want the result. Don't cancel just because a task is taking a while: substantial work can legitimately run for a long time, so prefer waiting on it (get_delegation_status with wait_ms) over canceling. If the task has already finished, nothing is canceled and its final result is returned instead.

name: check_user_feedback
description:
IMPORTANT: This tool gives you the ability to receive the user's real-time guidance while you work, preventing you from going down the wrong path and wasting effort. The user can type corrections, new requirements, or hints at any time during your turn — but you will NEVER see them unless you call this tool. Without it, you could spend minutes on work the user has already tried to redirect.

When to call:
- After thinking through your approach but BEFORE starting implementation — the user may have clarified requirements.
- Before making a significant decision (choosing an architecture, picking which files to modify, deciding on an approach) — the user may prefer a different direction.
- After completing a sub-task and before moving to the next step — the user may want to adjust priorities.
- When you pause to plan or organize your next steps — a natural checkpoint to read any pending guidance.

This is a quick, non-blocking snapshot that returns instantly. It either returns the user's messages (treat as HIGH-PRIORITY steering and adjust immediately) or an empty result (continue your current plan). Call it proactively — do not wait to be asked.

name: ask_user_question
description: Ask the user one or more multiple-choice questions and BLOCK until they answer. The questions render as interactive cards above the user's input box; this call returns only once the user submits their choices (or dismisses the card). Use ONLY when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make — one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults (e.g. which approach, which format, which library, which of several files). Do NOT use it to ask 'should I proceed?' or to confirm an obvious default, and do NOT use it for open-ended questions that aren't a small set of discrete choices. The user can always pick 'Other' and type a custom answer, so don't add your own 'Other' option. If you want to recommend a choice, put it first and append ' (Recommended)' to its label. Prefer ONE call with a few related questions over many sequential calls.

questions.description: 1-4 questions to ask in this single call.

question.description: The full question shown to the user.

header.description: Short category label (≤ 12 chars) shown as a chip, e.g. 'Approach', 'Format'.

multiSelect.description: If true, the user may select multiple options; otherwise it's a single choice.

label.description: Concise choice text. Append ' (Recommended)' to the first option to recommend it.

description.description: What this choice means or its trade-off.

name: get_session_info
description: Look up a session/conversation the user referenced in their message and return what it is: its title, which agent ran it, its status, workspace folder, git branch, model, message count, and token-usage stats — and, on request, a compact view of its most recent messages. Call this whenever the user's message contains a `iyw-claw://session/<number>` reference (a mentioned session) and you need to know what that session is about or what happened in it (e.g. to continue its work or summarize it). Pass the NUMBER from the reference as `session_id` (it is iyw-claw's internal conversation id, NOT the agent's own session id). The result is read-only and never modifies the session. A session that no longer exists returns a `found: false` result you can act on — it is not an error.

session_id.description: The number in the `iyw-claw://session/<number>` reference from the user's message (iyw-claw's internal conversation id). For example, given `[Fix auth](iyw-claw://session/214)`, pass 214.

max_messages.description: How many of the session's most recent turns to include as compact text. Defaults to 20; pass 0 for metadata only (faster, no transcript read). Capped at 200.

name: transcribe_audio
description: Transcribe a workspace-relative audio file in MP3, WAV/WAVE, OGG/OGA/Opus, MP4/M4A/M4B, or raw PCM format. The host uploads the file directly to managed storage, submits an asynchronous transcription job, and waits briefly for a result. Returns the transcript when ready, otherwise the jobId and status. Do not pass an absolute path, URL, bucket key, provider, or credentials.

path.description: Supported audio file path relative to the current workspace.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 language tag. Defaults to zh-CN.

name: query_audio_transcription
description: Query a previously returned audio transcription job. Use this after transcribe_audio returns a non-terminal status.

job_id.description: Decimal transcription job ID returned by transcribe_audio.

name: show_image
description: Display one image directly in the iyw-claw conversation. Supports a local file path, HTTP/HTTPS URL, Data URI, or raw Base64 with mime_type.

source.description: Local image path, file URI, HTTP/HTTPS URL, Data URI, or raw Base64 image data.

mime_type.description: Image MIME type. Required when source is raw Base64.

caption.description: Optional caption shown with the image.

name: analyze_image
description: Read and analyze an image using the current model's configured image-understanding route. Use this when an image is not already available as native visual input or when you need to inspect image details.

source.description: Local image path, file URI, HTTPS URL, Data URI, or raw Base64 image data.

question.description: The specific question to answer about the image.

mime_type.description: Required when source is raw Base64; optional for files and URLs.

name: append_user_memory
description: Append one durable, cross-task fact or preference that the user clearly stated to iyw-claw's user memory. Use this only when the information will remain useful in future conversations. Never store secrets, credentials, inferred sensitive traits, repository facts, temporary progress, or one-off task details. This tool is append-only: it cannot overwrite user memory and cannot modify the user's profile or soul documents.

content.description: A concise, standalone fact or preference explicitly provided by the user. Do not include Markdown structure, secrets, temporary task state, or speculation.

name: propose_user_memory
description: Submit one conservative candidate when the user explicitly gives a reusable correction, preference, or fact but has not clearly asked for permanent storage. This records an observation for later confirmation; it does not update active memory. Never submit secrets, inferred sensitive traits, repository facts, temporary progress, one-off task details, or agent reflections, and never claim that a proposal is already remembered.

content.description: A concise, standalone reusable statement explicitly grounded in the user's current message.

signal.description: The explicit user signal that motivated this candidate.

name: list_message_channels
description: List iyw-claw message channels using safe, non-secret views. Omit filters to list all channels. This never returns credentials, raw provider target ids, or config JSON.

name: save_message_channel
description: Create or patch an iyw-claw message channel. Omit channel_id to create. Supplied credential and provider bootstrap fields are write-only and are never returned. This executes immediately without confirmation.

channel_id.description: Existing channel id to patch. Omit to create.

channel_type.description: Required when creating and immutable afterwards.

daily_report_time.description: Daily report time in the format accepted by iyw-claw.

config.description: Typed partial configuration. Provider identifiers in this object are write-only bootstrap values.

credential.description: Optional write-only credential. Never echoed or stored in tool audit details.

name: delete_message_channel
description: Request deletion of one message channel and its local related records. The operation blocks until the user explicitly confirms or cancels it in iyw-claw.

reason.description: Optional reason for audit context; do not include secrets.

name: manage_channel_credential
description: Check, write, replace, delete, or run QR authorization for a channel credential. Credential values are write-only. Delete blocks for explicit user confirmation; other operations execute immediately.

request_id.description: Required for set, replace, delete, and start_authorization.

credential.description: Write-only credential for set or replace.

authorization_id.description: Opaque id returned by start_authorization; required for check_authorization.

name: operate_message_channel
description: Connect, disconnect, or diagnose an existing message channel. Results contain only normalized readiness and safe errors.

name: list_channel_targets
description: List safe opaque targets for one channel. Only configured defaults and conversations that really interacted with iyw-claw are returned. Use target_id from this tool when sending.

name: list_channel_messages
description: Read a bounded page of iyw-claw's local message log for one channel. This does not fetch platform history and never returns raw provider ids, full attachment paths, credentials, or unbounded bodies.

target_id.description: Optional opaque target id from list_channel_targets.

cursor.description: Opaque stable next_cursor returned by a previous page.

name: send_channel_messages
description: Send text or structured messages, optionally with readable local files, to default or known targets. target_id must come from list_channel_targets. File paths may be absolute or relative to the current Agent working directory. Unsupported attachments are reported per item and never disguised as successful sends.

request_id.description: Caller-generated idempotency id for the full batch.

target_id.description: Opaque default or known target id from list_channel_targets.

name: manage_channel_settings
description: Read or patch global message-channel settings. get returns only safe projections. Webhook URLs and routing secrets are write-only where applicable; patch executes immediately without confirmation.

api_key.description: Optional write-only natural-router credential. Never returned.

delete_api_key.description: Set true to remove the stored natural-router credential.
